sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: American beech is a deciduous tree of eastern Canada and the United States, usually 15–24 m tall. Its crown can be as wide as the tree is tall.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Separate male and female flowers appear on the same tree in spring. Two triangular beechnuts about 2 cm long ripen inside a spiny cupule. They are smaller than those of European beech (Fagus sylvatica), whose leaves are also smaller.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The nuts are eaten raw or cooked in small quantities; the horticultural sources consulted do not recommend eating large amounts.
